/-!
# Conjecture 5.15

by F. B. Cannonito

Do there exist finitely presented residually finite groups with recursive, but not
primitive recursive, solution of the word problem?

A finitely presented group is given by finitely many generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ and
finitely many relators. Its word problem is the set of words over the alphabet
$x_0^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_{n-1}^{\pm 1}$ that represent the identity element. By the
McKinsey–Mal'cev theorem, finitely presented residually finite groups have decidable
(recursive) word problem; the question is whether the word problem can fail to be
primitive recursive. Whether the word problem is (primitive) recursive does not depend on
the chosen finite presentation, since a change of finite presentation induces a primitive
recursive substitution on words. Hence the formalisation quantifies over finite
presentations.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

some normal subgroup of finite index, i.e. $g$ has non-trivial image in some finite quotient

blocks.name: IsResiduallyFinite
blocks.text:
/-- A group $G$ is residually finite if every non-identity element $g \in G$ lies outside
some normal subgroup of finite index, i.e. $g$ has non-trivial image in some finite quotient
of $G$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

blocks.code:
def WordProblem {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) (w : List (Fin n × Bool)) : Prop :=
  PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1
blocks.docstring:
The word problem of the group $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid \mathrm{rels} \rangle$
presented by `rels`: the predicate on words `w` over the alphabet
$x_0^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_{n-1}^{\pm 1}$ (encoded as lists of pairs `(i, b)`, where `b = true`
stands for $x_i$ and `b = false` for $x_i^{-1}$) that holds when `w` represents the identity
element of the presented group.

justification.closest_existing_considered: PresentedGroup.mk_eq_one_iff / Subgroup.normalClosure membership on FreeGroup (no Primcodable instance on FreeGroup, so not directly usable with PrimrecPred).
justification.name: Kourovka.«5.15».WordProblem
justification.why_needed: No word-problem notion exists in Mathlib or the repo. Defined as the predicate on words w : List (Fin n × Bool) given by PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1. Words (rather than FreeGroup elements) are used because List (Fin n × Bool) carries the standard Primcodable instance required by ComputablePred/PrimrecPred, whereas FreeGroup has none; this also matches the literal meaning of 'word problem'.

claims.decomposer_note: Single unlettered yes/no existence question (answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ G, ...): G must be finitely presented and residually finite, its word problem (the set of words over a finite generating set representing the identity) must be decidable/recursive — which is automatic for finitely presented residually finite groups by McKinsey–Mal'cev — but must not be decidable by any primitive recursive function; this complexity notion is independent of the chosen finite presentation, so the formalization should quantify over (or fix) a finite presentation without loss of generality, and care is needed to phrase 'primitive recursive decidability' of a word-problem set (Mathlib has Nat.Primrec / Primrec / Computable, ComputablePred) rather than of the group itself.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same mathematical content: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ finite presentation ⟨Fin n | rels⟩ (rels finite) such that PresentedGroup rels is residually finite and the word problem (words List (Fin n × Bool) mapping to 1 under FreeGroup.mk then PresentedGroup.mk) is ComputablePred but not PrimrecPred. I verified: Mathlib's PrimrecPred/ComputablePred existentially quantify the DecidablePred (so no classical-instance trap); Primcodable instances exist for List (Fin n × Bool) and the Mathlib list/pair encoding is primitive-recursively interconvertible with standard Gödel numberings of words, so 'primitive recursive word problem' has its classical meaning; FreeGroup.mk uses (a, true) = x_a, (a, false) = x_a⁻¹; fixing the presentation is WLOG since (primitive) recursiveness of the word problem is presentation-independent; residual finiteness via finite-index normal subgroups is the standard definition; no vacuity issues (existential with all conjuncts). c01 chosen as base: correct Mathlib naming (Prop-valued WordProblem in UpperCamelCase, unlike c02/c08's wordProblem), concise test lemmas for both bespoke definitions, AMS 3 20, thorough docstrings. Edits: added c02/c08's API lemma wordProblem_iff_mem_normalClosure (renamed for the WordProblem def) as a sanity check of the word-problem definition, and a sentence in the module docstring justifying presentation-independence. c08's extra sorry'd 'research solved' McKinsey–Mal'cev theorem was deliberately not included (outside the slot). c04's abstract-G formulation with a generating tuple is also faithful but more complex than needed; c07's Perm (Fin m) encoding of residual finiteness is correct but obscure; c03/c05/c06 are faithful but inline the predicate and lack tests/documentation.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.15

by F. B. Cannonito

Do there exist finitely presented residually finite groups with recursive, but not
primitive recursive, solution of the word problem?

A finitely presented group is given by finitely many generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ and
finitely many relators. Its word problem is the set of words over the alphabet
$x_0^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_{n-1}^{\pm 1}$ that represent the identity element. By the
McKinsey–Mal'cev theorem, finitely presented residually finite groups have decidable
(recursive) word problem; the question is whether the word problem can fail to be
primitive recursive. Whether the word problem is (primitive) recursive does not depend on
the chosen finite presentation, since a change of finite presentation induces a primitive
recursive substitution on words. Hence the formalisation quantifies over finite
presentations.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.15»

/-- A group $G$ is residually finite if every non-identity element $g \in G$ lies outside
some normal subgroup of finite index, i.e. $g$ has non-trivial image in some finite quotient
of $G$. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- The word problem of the group $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid \mathrm{rels} \rangle$
presented by `rels`: the predicate on words `w` over the alphabet
$x_0^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_{n-1}^{\pm 1}$ (encoded as lists of pairs `(i, b)`, where `b = true`
stands for $x_i$ and `b = false` for $x_i^{-1}$) that holds when `w` represents the identity
element of the presented group. -/
def WordProblem {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) (w : List (Fin n × Bool)) : Prop :=
  PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1

/-- Every finite group is residually finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isResiduallyFinite_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun g hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

/-- A word represents the identity of the presented group if and only if the corresponding
element of the free group lies in the normal closure of the relators. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem wordProblem_iff_mem_normalClosure {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))
    (w : List (Fin n × Bool)) :
    WordProblem rels w ↔ FreeGroup.mk w ∈ Subgroup.normalClosure rels :=
  PresentedGroup.mk_eq_one_iff

/-- The empty word represents the identity. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem wordProblem_nil {n : ℕ} (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) : WordProblem rels [] :=
  map_one _

/--
Do there exist finitely presented residually finite groups with recursive, but not
primitive recursive, solution of the word problem?

That is, is there a finite presentation $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid \mathrm{rels} \rangle$
(with $\mathrm{rels}$ finite) of a residually finite group whose word problem, as a predicate on
words over $x_0^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_{n-1}^{\pm 1}$, is decidable (`ComputablePred`) but is not
decidable by a primitive recursive function (`PrimrecPred`)? Primitive recursiveness is taken
with respect to the standard `Primcodable` encoding of words as elements of `List (Fin n × Bool)`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.15» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧
      IsResiduallyFinite (PresentedGroup rels) ∧
      ComputablePred (WordProblem rels) ∧ ¬ PrimrecPred (WordProblem rels) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.15»

items: The statement quantifies over finite presentations (n generators, finite relator set) rather than over abstract groups with an IsFinitelyPresented predicate; since the (primitive) recursiveness of the word problem is invariant under change of finite presentation, this is equivalent to the informal existence question (as the decomposition notes allow).

'Recursive solution of the word problem' is rendered as Mathlib's ComputablePred (decidable set of words); 'primitive recursive' as Mathlib's PrimrecPred. Both are relative to the standard Primcodable encoding of List (Fin n × Bool) (Primcodable.list over Primcodable.prod/fin/bool); primitive recursive predicates are closed under primitive-recursive re-encodings, so the choice of standard encoding does not affect the statement.
The redundant hypothesis ComputablePred (automatic by McKinsey–Mal'cev for f.p. residually finite groups) is kept because the source statement explicitly includes 'recursive'.
Residual finiteness is defined via finite-index normal subgroups (equivalently, separation by homomorphisms to finite groups) to avoid universe quantification over finite groups.
Two short @[category test] lemmas (finite groups are residually finite; the empty word is in the word problem) were added as basic API tests for the bespoke definitions, per CONTRIBUTING.md.

reviewer_notes: Problem is a single yes/no existence question; no ambiguity found in the source. The ComputablePred conjunct is redundant (McKinsey–Mal'cev: f.p. residually finite groups have decidable word problem) but kept to mirror the source's 'recursive, but not primitive recursive'. Universe: PresentedGroup rels lives in Type, matching the repository's practice of quantifying groups in Type. Only remaining modeling assumption is the standard one that 'primitive recursive solution of the word problem' refers to the set of words (over a finite generating set, in Mathlib's Primcodable encoding) being a primitive recursive set; this is invariant under change of finite presentation and under primitive-recursive re-encodings, so the choice is WLOG. File compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning; intended path FormalConjectures/Kourovka/5_15.lean.
